summary: Johnson County fire tower on the Pleasant Hill Ranger District, built around 1914; a 1938 paper reports a keeper moving to it. Its condition now is not described.

access.note: Reached by Forest Service road FSR 1432A; a trail listing describes a high-clearance route, and a user review warns not to drive past an old gate on the way up.

events.note: Trail listing says constructed around 1914; a Forest Service post shows the tower in 1914.
Mayford Huffines moved with his family from the Matney Knob tower to keep Devil's Knob tower, per the Baxter Bulletin of October 7, 1938, as quoted by Central US Lookouts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives the older Ozark National Forest name. The Forest Service post names the Ouachita and Ozark-St Francis National Forests, and the story uses Ozark-St. Francis.

notes_for_editor: No source we read confirms the tower's condition now. A YouTube search snippet (not fetched, so not cited) describes foundations around the old fire tower, which would suggest the tower may be gone; check on site or with the Forest Service before publishing. The 1914 date is 'around' per the trail listing and the Forest Service caption. A travel blog mentions 1920s architecture on the route without naming the tower, so it is not used. Do not confuse with the Devil's Knob natural area in Izard County (Arkansas Land Conservancy), which is a different site.
